issues.description: Nested relative color in accept test may not actually exercise the inner function's hue check
issues.detail: The accept case `oklch(from hsl(270deg 60% 50%) l c h)` only verifies the outer call. A reject test with a nested relative color whose inner function has a non-deg hue (e.g., `oklch(from hsl(270 60% 50%) l c h)`) would confirm recursion into nested function args still works correctly with the new offset logic.

In the HUE_FIRST_ARG_FUNCS branch, `args[0 + offset]` could simply be `args[offset]`. Minor readability nit; keeping symmetry with `args[2 + offset]` is the only argument for current form, but a brief comment or `args[offset]` would be clearer.

issues.description: Missing coverage for `lab`/`lch` relative-color variants in accept list
issues.detail: Tests cover `lch(from red 1 1 1deg)` but not `lab` (which isn't a hue function, so N/A) and not the symmetric `lch(from red l c h)` channel-name case. Adding `lch(from red l c h)` would mirror the oklch accept case and lock in HUE_THIRD_ARG_FUNCS behavior.

issues.description: Potential undefined `.value` access if args[0] is a non-standard node
issues.detail: `args[0]?.value.toLowerCase()` uses optional chaining on `args[0]` but not on `.value`. While postcss-value-parser word/function nodes always carry `.value`, defensive `args[0]?.value?.toLowerCase()` would prevent a TypeError if upstream parsing ever changes.

review.summary: The fix is small, well-targeted, and adds reasonable test coverage for the relative color syntax (`from <color>`) in `hsl`, `oklch`, and `lch`. Logic correctly offsets channel positions by 2 when the first arg is `from`, and handles uppercase via toLowerCase. Main gaps are test coverage edges: a reject case exercising a non-deg hue inside a nested relative color would lock in recursion behavior, and minor stylistic cleanups in the offset arithmetic. No P0 correctness issues spotted.
